nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: Snow has been falling on the Guild Hall of Steady Steps for three days, which it has never done before. It sits on the windowsills like icing, and Biscuit has declared war on it.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: {hero}! Come in, shake off the snow. Not on the Duck Mat. Never on the Duck Mat.

nodes.speaker: maple
nodes.text: The door has been open since noon and everything is damp. I stopped counting puddles at nineteen.

nodes.speaker: pip
nodes.text: I have been mopping. The puddles are winning. I don't mind, though. It's nice, being busy because the hall is busy.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: The door bangs. Somebody comes through it at a run, stops very suddenly, and slides the whole length of the hall on the wet floor, red scarf arriving a moment later.

nodes.speaker: fennel
nodes.text: Post! Post for the Guild Hall! Is this the Guild Hall? It is. Sorry about the floor! I'm Fennel!

nodes.speaker: pip
nodes.text: Whoa. Are you all right?

nodes.speaker: fennel
nodes.text: Fine! I only fall over at the end of a run. It keeps things tidy.

nodes.speaker: maple
nodes.text: There is now a Fennel-shaped puddle. Tidy is not the word.

nodes.speaker: fennel
nodes.text: I'm a courier from Thunder Heights, up beyond the pass. This is the first letter to make it down in two winters. I have been practising the speech all the way and now every word has left.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: Fennel pulls a damp envelope from the satchel. It is sealed with a blob of blue wax in the shape of a very small bell.

nodes.prompt: What do you do for Fennel?

reply.speaker: maple
reply.text: Tea. With honey. Sit. Not on the Duck Mat.

reply.speaker: fennel
reply.text: I don't think I've sat in a hall for two winters. It's very... flat. I like it.

options.label: Ask them to catch a breath.

reply.speaker: fennel
reply.text: Right. Breath. One... two... I've never done this on purpose before. It's actually quite good.

reply.speaker: pip
reply.text: It really is. I do it before I walk into a room.

reply.speaker: fennel
reply.text: Yes! Together! That's the best idea anyone has had since I arrived, and I arrived forty seconds ago.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: 'To the Guild Hall that rang the Dawn Bell, and to the light that answered it.' Oh, that's lovely. Somebody up there has been listening.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: {hero} lit the great lamp with one careful spark, and it carried all the way up a mountain. Good sparks do that.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: We lit that lamp together, in a heap, with nobody doing it tidily. It must have been very bright.

nodes.speaker: pip
nodes.text: They saw the lamp I lit. From a mountain! I'm going to need to lie down for a bit. Then tell everyone.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: 'The Weather Chime, which sings the day's weather down to the high farms, has not sounded in two winters. The storms have been loud ever since. We do not ask for rescue. The kettle is on, and there is a great deal of stair.'

nodes.speaker: maple
nodes.text: The pass is shut in winter for a reason, Chad. Nothing here has a deadline. We pack properly and go slowly.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: Slowly! Yes! The one thing a mountain can't do is hurry us. I will pack the cape.

nodes.speaker: maple
nodes.text: You will pack the second pair of socks.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: ...I will pack the second pair of socks.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: By evening the hall smells of wet wool and plans, and the road north is as white as a clean page.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: The road north climbs in long, wide zigzags between pines wearing snow like very large hats.

nodes.speaker: fennel
nodes.text: Right! Shortcut! If we go straight up the gully we skip four bends, and... hold on. Where did the gully go?

nodes.speaker: pip
nodes.text: It's behind you. You walked past it.

nodes.speaker: fennel
nodes.text: I walk past things at speed. It's a talent. It has never once been useful.

nodes.speaker: brad
nodes.text: {hero}! I heard there was a mountain! I have brought a rope, two flasks, a flag, and a second flag in case the first one gets lonely.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: Brad, there is nobody to plant the flag on yet.

nodes.speaker: brad
nodes.text: I like to be ready. I also rested before we left. I'm very good at it now. Ask anyone.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: He is. It's annoying.

nodes.speaker: fennel
nodes.text: Serious question. How do you all go up a hill? Because I've only got one speed and it's 'fast, then fall over'.

options.label: Steady, a step at a time.

reply.speaker: narrator
reply.text: You settle into a rhythm: a step, a breath, a step. The hill, which was expecting an argument, seems almost pleased.

reply.speaker: brad
reply.text: A rhythm! I have one of those. Mine is mostly humming.

reply.speaker: narrator
reply.text: You climb in bursts and stop at every bend to look back. By the third bend the whole valley lies below like a map.

reply.speaker: fennel
reply.text: That's... basically how I run. But I thought bursts didn't count.

reply.speaker: pip
reply.text: They count. Bursts count.

reply.speaker: narrator
reply.text: Steep bit, short steps. Flat bit, a stretch of the legs. You let the hill choose, and the hill turns out to be a very reasonable guide.

reply.speaker: chad
reply.text: I've always said mountains give excellent advice. It's their only job.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: Halfway up the second slope, Fennel's pace drops to something nearly human. Pip falls into step beside them.

nodes.speaker: pip
nodes.text: Someone told me once that the wall counts. Even if all you do is get to the wall. I think about it a lot.

nodes.speaker: pip
nodes.text: Someone told me once to rest at every landing. I still do. Nobody has ever been annoyed. Not once.

nodes.speaker: pip
nodes.text: Someone once climbed a hundred and eighty-two steps right beside me, so I know what that's worth. We'll go beside you, Fennel.

nodes.speaker: fennel
nodes.text: I've never been looked after on a hill. I'm usually dropping the post and gone before the kettle boils.

nodes.speaker: brad
nodes.text: Go at your own pace, Fennel. The mountain isn't timing anybody. I checked. It has no watch.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: First rule of hills: everybody takes them differently, and they all arrive at the top. Eventually. Mostly with snacks.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: Pip, who a season ago clutched a mat like a shield, takes the lead where the road narrows. They know exactly where the next bend is, and they wait for everyone at it.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: Past noon the sky turns the colour of a pewter plate and the wind finds its voice. Then, round a bend, a small stone hut with a smoking chimney and a very large sign: STOP HERE. THIS MEANS YOU.

nodes.speaker: fennel
nodes.text: I've never stopped here. I always run straight past. I thought it was for... emergencies.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: 'This means you.' I do love a sign with confidence.

nodes.speaker: brad
nodes.text: I would like to stop. I'm excellent at it.

nodes.speaker: pip
nodes.text: It isn't us giving up. It's the sign telling us it's allowed.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: The door opens before anyone can knock. Warm light spills over the snow, along with a smell of barley and woodsmoke, and a very deep, very soft voice.

nodes.speaker: hush
nodes.text: Come in. Mind your heads. Mind mine, mostly.

nodes.speaker: hush
nodes.text: I am Hush. I keep the hut. There is soup. There is always soup. It is my whole job, and I am very good at it.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: A legendary profession. I've always said so.

nodes.speaker: fennel
nodes.text: You've been here the whole time? Two winters? I've run past this hut more times than I can count!

nodes.speaker: hush
nodes.text: I saw you. A scarf, going by. Every time, I put a mug on the step. You never saw.

nodes.speaker: fennel
nodes.text: The mugs! I thought the wind had left them! I've been stepping over mugs! For two winters!

nodes.speaker: hush
nodes.text: It is all right. The mugs kept. Some people need a long time before they are ready to stop. I keep the stove warm for all of them.

nodes.speaker: pip
nodes.text: That is the nicest thing I've ever heard anyone say.

nodes.speaker: hush
nodes.text: On a mountain, every path has a hut. Not because anyone is slow. A path with nowhere to sit is not really a path. It is only a hurry.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: Rest is training, Hush. It's on a banner.

nodes.speaker: hush
nodes.text: I know. Wren sent it over on a seagull. It is above the stove.

nodes.prompt: What soup do you ask for?

reply.speaker: hush
reply.text: A sturdy choice. A soup that tells you it will still be here tomorrow.

reply.speaker: hush
reply.text: Pepper! A person with ideas. Sit by the stove. The good chair is the one with the dent.

reply.speaker: hush
reply.text: Oh. Nobody ever lets me choose. ...Mushroom and barley, with a little honey. It is what I make when someone looks like they have come a long way.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: I once climbed a whole mountain in a single morning, and I'd like to tell you all about—

nodes.speaker: hush
nodes.text: Sit down, Chad.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: ...Sitting down.

nodes.speaker: hush
nodes.text: You will meet my cousins on the road, further up. They are shy, and announce it with their fists. They mean it kindly. Take a scarf.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: The scarf is enormous, striped, and smells of woodsmoke. Outside the wind howls and the snow comes down, and inside there is soup, and no one is going anywhere for a little while.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: The road narrows to a cut in the ice, and the cut becomes a cave. Everything is blue. The pillars shine. Even the sound seems blue.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: Something small and green pops out from behind an icicle with a large sack.

nodes.speaker: grit
nodes.text: BUTTONS! There are buttons in the walls! Thousands! ...Oh. They're crystals. They're still wonderful!

nodes.speaker: grit
nodes.text: I heard there was a mountain and I thought, a mountain must have the best shiny things. I've been here three days. I have never been so happy.

nodes.speaker: fennel
nodes.text: Echo test! Hello!

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: '...hello,' says the cave, a moment later, a little softer.

nodes.speaker: brad
nodes.text: I AM BRAD!

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: '...am Brad,' says the cave, gently, as though pleased to meet him.

nodes.speaker: grit
nodes.text: It says things back! It says them back NICELY!

nodes.speaker: pip
nodes.text: I read that ice caves do this. They give your voice back a bit slower, so you have time to hear it.

nodes.speaker: fennel
nodes.text: I'm... not very good at slow. And I don't say much out loud. I'm usually gone before anyone asks.

nodes.speaker: pip
nodes.text: Try something you don't usually say. Or just say hello. It's allowed.

nodes.prompt: What do you say to the cave?

reply.speaker: narrator
reply.text: '...doing my best,' the cave says, slowly, and once more, quieter: 'my best.' It sounds like something worth hearing twice.

reply.speaker: narrator
reply.text: '...a good climb,' the cave agrees. For a moment nobody says anything at all. It was.

reply.speaker: narrator
reply.text: 'Hello, cave,' says the cave.

reply.speaker: grit
reply.text: It said hello back! We're friends! I'm going to name a crystal after it!

nodes.speaker: fennel
nodes.text: Okay. My turn. I always run so nobody asks if I'm all right. ...I'm doing my best.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: '...doing my best,' says the cave.

nodes.speaker: fennel
nodes.text: It sounded nicer coming back. Why does it sound nicer coming back?

nodes.speaker: pip
nodes.text: That's the cave's trick. It only repeats what you give it. It just says it slowly enough to believe.

nodes.speaker: brad
nodes.text: I'd like it noted that I said 'I am Brad' and the cave agreed with me.

nodes.speaker: grit
nodes.text: Here. I found you a shiny. It is a button. It was always going to be a button.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: They leave the cave with their pockets full of blue light, and Fennel walks out, actually walks, hands in pockets, looking at the ceiling.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: At the head of the pass the road ends at a stone tower. A great many stairs wind around it like ribbon. At the bottom, on a folding chair, a woman in a long blue coat is drinking from a thermos and looking up.

nodes.speaker: tamsin
nodes.text: You'll be the guild. I heard the bell. Both times. Welcome to the foot of my stair. I'd say come up, but I'm told that's rude.

nodes.speaker: fennel
nodes.text: Tamsin! I got the letter down! It took two winters and a very wet hall!

nodes.speaker: tamsin
nodes.text: Fennel. You stopped, didn't you? For soup. I'm so proud I've gone quiet.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: Madam Weatherkeeper! Your tower! Your Chime! Your... chair?

nodes.speaker: tamsin
nodes.text: Four hundred and twelve steps. I used to take them two at a time with a kettle. Then one hard winter I came down, and I haven't gone up since.

nodes.speaker: tamsin
nodes.text: It isn't that I can't. It's that I stopped, and every day I didn't climb, the stair got a little taller.

nodes.speaker: pip
nodes.text: I know that stair. For me it was a wall. Every day I didn't try, it got higher. Then somebody said the wall counts.

nodes.prompt: What do you say to Tamsin?

options.label: Let me sit with you a while.

reply.speaker: tamsin
reply.text: Ah. Sitting. I am excellent at that. It's the one thing I definitely haven't forgotten.

reply.speaker: narrator
reply.text: You pull up a rock beside her. For a while nobody needs to say anything, and the wind goes round the tower like a cat.

reply.speaker: tamsin
reply.text: One step. That's a suspiciously small number.

reply.speaker: pip
reply.text: It's a number you can do. That's what makes it a good one.

reply.speaker: tamsin
reply.text: The view! Oh, the view. On a clear night you can see a lamp on a far headland, and a bell on a green hill, and a little smoke from a hut.

reply.speaker: tamsin
reply.text: I haven't seen it from the top in a long while. I think I've missed it more than the stair.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: Tamsin folds up the chair, and puts down the thermos, and puts one boot on the bottom step. It is a small step. She looks at it as though it were the biggest thing on the mountain.

nodes.speaker: tamsin
nodes.text: One.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: Is that all?

nodes.speaker: pip
nodes.text: One counts.

nodes.speaker: tamsin
nodes.text: My teacher used to say it. 'Rest is training.' I'd run up the stair out of embarrassment, just to prove him wrong.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: He was right. It's on a banner.

nodes.speaker: fennel
nodes.text: Take the landings. Take all of them. I'll sit with you at every one. I'm getting good at it.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: At the first landing, twelve steps up, Tamsin sits down on the cold stone with a long breath, and Fennel sits down beside her, and nobody runs anywhere.

nodes.speaker: tamsin
nodes.text: The second landing tomorrow. Or the day after. The Chime has waited two winters. Nothing here has a deadline.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: Below them lie the pass, the road, and the thin grey line of Hush's smoke. Tamsin looks at all of it for a long time.

nodes.speaker: tamsin
nodes.text: Funny. From here it looks so much shorter. It was always this short. I just wasn't standing on it.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: It takes many days to climb the stair, with a landing for every sit and a sit for every landing. Nobody counts the days. Tamsin counts the steps, under her breath, and on the last one she says a word that is in no guidebook.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: At the top the wind is loud and the clouds are low. In the middle of the platform hangs a great iron ring of seven bells, perfectly silent. Beneath it sits a very small person under a very large thundercloud.

nodes.speaker: skarn
nodes.text: Go away! ...Please. Sorry. Go away, please.

nodes.speaker: pip
nodes.text: Are you... making the storm?

nodes.speaker: skarn
nodes.text: I'm not MAKING it. It just comes out when I'm upset. Which is always, now.

nodes.speaker: tamsin
nodes.text: Skarn. Little Skarn.

nodes.speaker: skarn
nodes.text: Tamsin?! You came UP?! I didn't mean it! I rang one wrong note, and then you stopped coming, and I thought if I made it loud enough you'd hear it from down there and—

nodes.speaker: tamsin
nodes.text: Oh, love. You didn't make me stop. I made me stop. It had nothing to do with you.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: I have a speech about storms. It's very moving. It has a goose in it.

nodes.speaker: skarn
nodes.text: Please no.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: ...Fair.

nodes.prompt: What do you say to Skarn?

reply.speaker: skarn
reply.text: Everybody says that. ...But you said it like it was true. Nobody says it like it's true.

options.label: Would you like a hot drink?

reply.speaker: skarn
reply.text: I'd like that very much. I haven't had one in a long time. I forgot you could just ask.

reply.speaker: fennel
reply.text: I have Hush's flask. It's been waiting for someone to need it.

reply.speaker: skarn
reply.text: Really? You want to see it? I didn't think anyone... Okay. Okay! It's very beautiful, if you're not scared of it.

nodes.speaker: tamsin
nodes.text: The Chime is rung by two. One for the low bells, one for the high. Skarn took the high ones. He always had the better ear.

nodes.speaker: skarn
nodes.text: And then I thought, if I ring them alone it'll be wrong again. And the weather comes out as whatever I'm feeling. And I'm feeling... rather a lot.

nodes.speaker: tamsin
nodes.text: Then we'll ring them together. But not tonight, love. Tonight we eat something and go to sleep.

nodes.speaker: skarn
nodes.text: It doesn't have to be tonight? You promise? The Chime isn't cross?

nodes.speaker: tamsin
nodes.text: Bells are never cross. They are only waiting. They're extremely good at it.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: The storm does not go away. But something in it softens, the way a loud voice does when someone finally asks it what's wrong. The thunder rolls over to one side and sits down.

nodes.speaker: pip
nodes.text: Can we put a roof on that cloud? Just so it's cosy?

nodes.speaker: skarn
nodes.text: ...You can try. It's quite shy.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: That night the clouds lie far below like a second ground, silver in the moonlight. A green light ripples across the sky. In the middle of the platform burns one small, determined fire.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: I'll tell you a thing I've never told. One winter I did nothing. Absolutely nothing. By spring I was certain I would have to start again from the very bottom.

nodes.speaker: brad
nodes.text: I remember. You had a cold. You told everyone it was a quest.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: Do you know what I did on my first day back? Two push-ups. ...They were the best two push-ups of my life.

nodes.speaker: brad
nodes.text: I counted three.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: You counted two. You're very supportive.

nodes.speaker: tamsin
nodes.text: I used to think coming back was starting over. It isn't. It's picking up where the stair has been waiting for you.

nodes.speaker: skarn
nodes.text: What if I ring it wrong tomorrow? What if it's a terrible afternoon?

nodes.speaker: tamsin
nodes.text: Then the weather will be silly for an afternoon, and we'll try again. That's the whole secret of bells.

nodes.prompt: What do you share by the fire?

reply.speaker: tamsin
reply.text: Good. Say it out loud. Things you are proud of should be said out loud at least once.

reply.speaker: pip
reply.text: I'm proud of you for saying it. That counts for two.

reply.speaker: skarn
reply.text: Me too. I'm learning how to ring a bell without it being the end of the world.

reply.speaker: chad
reply.text: A hard one. I'm still learning to sit through a soup without a speech.

reply.speaker: tamsin
reply.text: That's a perfectly good thing to share. Fires are good at that. They never ask for more.

nodes.speaker: fennel
nodes.text: I used to think delivering things fast was the only way to matter. I stopped, Pip. Three times this week. And somehow I've delivered more than I ever did.

nodes.speaker: pip
nodes.text: I used to think everyone knew exactly what they were doing. Then somebody told me they'd just been doing it longer.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: That's the first rule of the hall. It's on the board, next to the one about the kettle.

nodes.speaker: brad
nodes.text: I counted the stars. Eleven. Twelve, if you count the one I'm sure about.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: Far below the cloud sea, tiny lights prick through: a lamp on a far headland, a bell tower on a green hill, a little glow where a stove burns in a hut.

nodes.speaker: skarn
nodes.text: I never saw them from up here. I was looking down at my feet so hard.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: Skarn falls asleep sitting up. His little cloud has stopped thundering. It is snoring. It lets fall one snowflake at a time.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: Morning comes up gold over a sea of cloud, and the seven bells hang waiting. The wind is hardly there at all.

nodes.speaker: skarn
nodes.text: I'm going to be sick. In a weather way. There might be hail.

nodes.speaker: tamsin
nodes.text: There might. If there is, we'll all stand under the Chime and wait for it to pass.

nodes.speaker: brad
nodes.text: I brought an umbrella. And a second umbrella.

nodes.speaker: pip
nodes.text: In case the first one gets lonely?

nodes.speaker: brad
nodes.text: I'm learning from you, Pip.

nodes.prompt: How do you start the Chime?

reply.speaker: tamsin
reply.text: Low bells first, then. Skarn, you'll hear where you come in. You always did.

reply.speaker: skarn
reply.text: Me? First? ...Okay. Okay. I know the first note. I've known it all along.

reply.speaker: tamsin
reply.text: Together, then. It's how it was always meant to be, I think. We just forgot to ask.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: The first bell sounds, low and warm. Then the second, and the third. The high bells answer, clear as spring water. Seven notes, and each one a different weather: sun, breeze, rain, snow, fog, thunder, and the quiet that comes after.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: The thundercloud over Skarn's head lets go of a long breath and comes apart like a dandelion. Light pours across the cloud sea.

nodes.speaker: skarn
nodes.text: It's... right. It's actually right.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: From out of the clouds, trotting briskly in a knitted coat three sizes too big, comes Biscuit. Nobody asks how. He seems to feel it is obvious.

nodes.speaker: fennel
nodes.text: He arrived at the pass post. Addressed to Chad. Stamped 'Fragile, Excellent.'

nodes.speaker: biscuit
nodes.text: *Woof!*

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: He says it's a fine mountain. I can't say I disagree with him.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: Then, far below and to the east, a deep, warm note rolls up through the clouds: BONG. The Dawn Bell, answering.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: And far to the west, on a headland too distant to see, something bright winks once in the morning light, the way a lamp does when it's saying hello.

nodes.speaker: tamsin
nodes.text: A bell for morning, a lamp for night, and a Chime for all the weather in between. We've waited a long time to be part of that.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: Skarn! The hall has room for a weather-wizard. The kettle's on, the Duck Mat is free, and Maple makes a terrifying scone.

nodes.speaker: skarn
nodes.text: Can I come? Sometimes? I don't think I can leave the Chime. ...Can the Chime come?

nodes.speaker: tamsin
nodes.text: You'll come down every spring, love, and I'll come down in autumn. By stages. Stopping at all the landings. I intend to take as long as it takes.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: Come by when you like, {hero}. Move however you like, rest when you need to, and bring the weather if you can't help it. The hall is yours.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: Come by when you like, {hero}. Have fun with it, the way you said you would. Bring a snowball. The hall is yours.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: Come by when you like, {hero}. Stay curious, the way you did from the very first day. There is always another path to wonder at. The hall is yours.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: The Chime sings, the bell answers, and the lamp winks. Between them lie a hundred places to sit down, and everyone, at their own pace, is on the way to one of them.
